title: How the query optimizer chooses a plan
description: Follow the step-by-step process SQL Server uses to parse, optimize, and select a query execution plan.

data.text: The query optimizer is a cost-based engine that evaluates many possible execution plans and selects the one it estimates will be cheapest in terms of CPU, memory, and I/O. Understanding how it works helps you recognize why a plan looks the way it does and how to influence it when it makes a poor choice.

data.title: What happens when a query arrives
items: Parsing: SQL Server checks syntax and builds an initial logical tree
Algebraic binding: The tree is converted into an internal query tree
Simplification: Redundant operations and constant expressions are removed
Trivial plan: For very simple queries, a cheap plan is chosen immediately
Full optimization: The optimizer explores alternative access paths, join orders, and join algorithms

data.text: During full optimization, the optimizer assigns a cost to each candidate plan based on estimated I/O, CPU, and memory requirements. The costs are not actual dollars or seconds; they are internal units used for relative comparison. The plan with the lowest estimated cost is chosen.

The optimizer does not examine every possible plan. For complex queries, the search space is enormous, so the optimizer uses heuristics and time limits to stop searching once a good enough plan is found. This means the optimizer can sometimes miss an optimal plan, especially for queries with many joins or unusual predicates.

data.title: The optimizer is not omniscient
data.text: SQL Server does not know your data distribution, business logic, or usage patterns in the same way you do. Hints, index design, and statistics are the main ways you guide the optimizer toward a better plan.

data.title: View the estimated plan without running
data.content: Ctrl+L in SSMS generates the estimated plan based on current statistics. Use it to see the optimizer's choices before touching production data.

data.caption: Simplified query optimization flow
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    A[Parse] --> B[Algebrize]
    B --> C[Simplify]
    C --> D{Trivial?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Trivial Plan]
    D -->|No| F[Optimize]
    F --> G[Choose Best Plan]
    G --> H[Execute]

data.title: Takeaway
points: The optimizer is cost-based, not rule-based
Costs are internal estimates for CPU, memory, and I/O
Time limits and heuristics stop the search early
Schema, indexes, and statistics are your main levers
data.takeaway: Think of the optimizer as a very fast but sometimes narrow-minded planner. Your job is to give it accurate statistics and good index options so it can choose well.
